links.targetTitle: The Resilience Fund can be used when Sky itself is the targe
Eligibility for the Resilience Fund is proven by onchain par

title: Whitehats must be legally named and pass KYC and sanctions screening, unlike the pseudonymous contributors the Atlas protects elsewhere
content:
A.2.11.1.2.2.3.2.4 offers three settings for the `identity` parameter — `0` Anonymous, `1` Pseudonymous, `2` Named — and Sky chooses `2`, requiring the whitehat's legal name. A.2.11.1.2.2.3.2.3 adds that all eligible whitehats "undergo Know Your Customer (KYC) verification and be screened against global sanctions lists, including OFAC, UK, and EU regulations," conducted "by a trusted third-party provider at Sky and Stars discretion, and all data is deleted, if successful, within 30 days post-verification."

The driver is sanctions exposure, not curiosity. Paying a bounty is paying a person; paying a sanctioned person is a violation that no amount of good intent cures, and Sky cannot screen an address alone.

The contrast with the rest of the Support Scope is stark and worth flagging. The Resilience Fund deliberately accepts pseudonymous beneficiaries through purely onchain Proof of Eligibility (A.2.9.1.1.1.4.1.1), and A.2.9.1.3 commits Sky to a framework maximizing "privacy, and pseudonymity for participants." Sky protects its own contributors' anonymity while requiring external rescuers to identify themselves.

The rationale for the split is defensible — beneficiaries receive defense funding for work already provably done onchain, while whitehats receive payment for conduct that must be legally clean. But the practical effect is selection: the researchers most capable of catching a live exploit are often the least willing to hand a legal identity to a third-party verifier, and the 30-day deletion promise is a policy commitment, not a technical guarantee.
description: The identity parameter is set to Named rather than Anonymous or Pseudonymous, with OFAC, UK and EU screening by a third party and deletion of data within 30 days of successful verification.
